drills.title: Revenue per region from CSV rows
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines so the program totals quantity x price per region from CSV text (the first line is the header). The map may be created before the list. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: Row 0 is the header, so the loop starts at subList(1, ...); otherwise parseInt would meet the text "qty" and crash. split(",") gives text cells, and text cannot be multiplied: convert each one with Integer.parseInt first. merge then adds to the old total of the region or starts a new one.

drills.title: One CSV row to revenue
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program splits one CSV row, converts the cells and prints the goal output.
drills.explain: split cuts the row into text cells (the -1 keeps empty cells at the end), and Integer.parseInt turns a cell into a number. Dividing by the int 100 would make 25 / 100 equal 0 and give no discount, so the divisor must be 100.0. String.join glues the items with a separator: how a CSV line is written.

drills.title: Empty cells and text cells
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: Without -1, split silently drops the empty cells at the end, so only North and 2 remain (2). With -1 all four cells are kept (4). Every cell is text: "4" + "100" glues them into 4100, and only after parseInt does + add them up to 104.

drills.title: The header is not a sale
drills.prompt: The program crashes while it runs. Click the faulty line, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: The first line of a CSV file holds the column names, so the loop meets the text "quantity" and parseInt throws NumberFormatException. subList(1, size) starts after the header. subList(0, size - 1) still contains the header, and subList(2, ...) would skip the first real sale and print a wrong total.

drills.title: Review the AI's sales report code
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this CSV code. It compiles and runs on the sample rows, but tick the real problems (there are three).
code: record Sale(String region, int quantity, int unitPrice, int discountPct) {
return new Sale(c[0], Integer.parseInt(c[1]), Integer.parseInt(c[2]), Integer.parseInt(c[3]));
static String toCsvLine(String name, double revenue) {

issues.text: discountPct / 100 is a whole-number division, so no discount is ever applied
issues.why: 25 / 100 is 0 in int arithmetic, so the North order is charged in full (the total is 2500.0, not 2000.0). Divide by 100.0.

issues.text: split(",") drops empty cells at the end of a row
issues.why: A row like North,2,1000, loses its last cell and c[3] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of being handled. split(",", -1) keeps every cell, so the problem can be reported properly.

issues.text: toCsvLine writes the name without quotes
issues.why: A name that contains a comma, such as Chai, masala, adds an extra cell and breaks the file. Wrap such a value in double quotes (and double any inner quotes).

non_issues.text: subList(1, lines.size()) skips the first sale
non_issues.why: Index 0 is the header line with the column names. Starting at 1 is exactly how a CSV loop avoids it.

non_issues.text: A record is not allowed to have a method such as revenue()
non_issues.why: Records may have methods. Only the fields are fixed.

non_issues.text: The cells must be converted with Double.parseDouble, not Integer.parseInt
non_issues.why: Quantity, unit price and discount are whole numbers in this file, so Integer.parseInt is the right conversion.

drills.explain: Generated CSV code usually works on the happy path. Check the numeric division, empty cells and special characters in values before you trust it with a real export.
